explain: Convert each hex digit to its own 4 bits: 1 = 0001 and 9 = 1001.

q: What is the decimal value of the single hex digit A?
explain: Hex counts 0–9, then A = 10, B = 11, C = 12, D = 13, E = 14, F = 15.

q: What is the decimal value 26 in two-digit hexadecimal?
explain: 26 in binary is 00011010. Group it as 0001 1010, which is 1A.

q: What is the decimal value 175 in two-digit hexadecimal?
explain: 175 in binary is 10101111. Group it as 1010 1111, which is AF.

q: What is the decimal value 200 in two-digit hexadecimal?
explain: 200 in binary is 11001000. Group it as 1100 1000, which is C8.

q: What is the decimal value 77 in two-digit hexadecimal?
explain: 77 in binary is 01001101. Group it as 0100 1101, which is 4D.

q: How many bits are in a MAC address?
explain: A MAC address is 48 bits, written as 12 hex digits in 6 pairs.

q: How many bits does one hexadecimal digit represent?
explain: Sixteen values (0–F) need exactly 4 bits, so one hex digit is always one 4-bit group.

q: In the MAC address 00:50:56:C0:00:08, which part identifies the manufacturer?
explain: The first 24 bits are the Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI) assigned to the manufacturer; the last 24 bits identify the individual interface.

q: How many hex digits are written in a MAC address?
explain: 48 bits divided by 4 bits per hex digit is 12 digits, usually shown as 6 pairs.

q: What is the largest value a single hex digit can hold?
explain: F is the last of the sixteen characters 0–F and equals 15, all four bits on.
